methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $5.7B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 1 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 2 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
The Boring Company, a Series G transportation venture founded by Elon Musk, carries a current post-money valuation of $5.7B after raising $675M to date. The relevant peer universe in Transportation is narrow: two private comparables are identifiable (Rivian and Einride), with no public peers available for direct benchmarking.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Applied to the $5.7B last post-money valuation, a 1.25x step-up multiplier—representative of typical Series G to subsequent-stage advancement—yields an implied valuation of $7.1B. Peer-median triangulation was not executable; while two same-sector peers exist, neither satisfied the minimum threshold of three comparables at matching or adjacent stage with similar valuation tier, making a narrow peer analysis unreliable and broader cross-sector medians inappropriate for transportation-specific risk profiles.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $6.1B (low) to $8.2B (high), centered at $7.1B. Key uncertainties limiting confidence include the insufficient peer dataset—reliance on one method rather than triangulation across multiple independent approaches—and the absence of public Transportation comps to anchor market-based benchmarking. The current $5.7B valuation sits meaningfully below the stage-adjusted median, which may reflect either a conservative round pricing or valuation compression in the private market. Resolution of these uncertainties would require expanded comparable data or bottom-up unit economics analysis.
